title: End the zero rate on electricity in April 2027
noun: ending the electricity zero rate early
headline: End electricity zero rate early. Raises £0.3bn in 2027-28, nothing by 2029-30.
description: VAT on domestic electricity is 0% from October 2026 to July 2027. Switch this on to end it in April 2027 instead, the first year you can change. It raises nothing by 2029-30, so this moves 2027-28 only.

baselinePolicy.text: VAT on domestic electricity is 0% from 1 October 2026 to 1 July 2027, then 5% (Table 6.1 line 2).

source.quote: This measure is effective from 1 October 2026 until 1 July 2027.

alreadyIncludes: VAT on domestic electricity is 0% from 1 October 2026 to 1 July 2027, then 5% (Table 6.1 line 2).

lines.title: Support for Energy Bills: Cut VAT on domestic electricity from 5% to 0% from 1 October 2026 to 1 July 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.
Only the first quarter of 2027-28 is yours to change: the half-year to March 2027 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.

interactions.text: One ends the zero rate early, the other keeps it going; the rate cannot do both.
